samples.input: Prove that among any 6 integers, two have the same remainder modulo 5.
samples.target: There are only 5 remainder classes modulo 5. By the pigeonhole principle, placing 6 integers into 5 classes forces at least one class to contain two integers.

samples.input: A process succeeds 9 times in 10 observed trials. Give three explanations for this rate and specify what additional evidence would separate skill from sampling noise.
samples.target: Possible explanations include a true success probability near 0.9, a lower true probability with a lucky sample, or selection/reporting bias. Separate them with a larger preregistered sample, known denominator, and independent replication.
